messages:
alex: quick heads-up — saw a weird regression on multi-GPU TP=8 inference runs after r3124. each rank holds ~1.8GB of persistent 'staging' / comm buffers across iterations, even when batch size is tiny. nvprof / nsight snapshots attached to the repro show repeated temp allocations that don't get freed between steps.

mira: ugh. could be the new allocator arenas not returning slabs to the device. did you see the change that made small temp allocs go into the staging pool?

alex: yep, looks like that. stack traces point to comm send/recv paths allocating tmp tensors for NCCL ops. nvprof sample:
```
malloc_device() -> staging_alloc() -> nccl_comm_prepare() -> kernel(...)
free_device() seems not called until stream sync + destructor delay
```

raj: hypothesis: allocator sticky behaviour + kv-cache hot pages = fragmentation + accumulation. when TP shards co-exist with kv cache, the allocator never triggers slab reclaim because live pointer scan marks those slabs as resident. result: temp allocs get appended to new slabs per-iteration.

sam: do we have numbers? perf-bot: can you post the regression snapshot?

perf-bot: baseline (r3109) TP=8 1K tokens: P99 latency 420ms, GPU mem avg 14.1GB. current (r3124): P99 472ms (+12.4%), GPU mem avg 15.9GB (+12.8%), OOMs on a few hosts when concurrency >6. Throughput down ~8%.

mira: ok. short-term mitigations: 1) reduce staging_pool_limit per-device, 2) enable slab_reclaim after N iterations, 3) force temp_pool_reuse=true so repeated temps reuse the same buffer instead of allocating new slabs.

raj: longer term: change allocator to epoch-based eviction for staging buffers used by NCCL. idea: mark dedicated staging allocations as "ephemeral-epoch" and reclaim them at epoch boundaries independent of live-pointer scans. simplifies interaction with KV cache since KV pages stay pinned but staging can be released.

sam: any concerns with NCCL semantics? will freeing buffers mid-run cause races?

mira: need to ensure we only reclaim buffers that are not outstanding on any comm stream. plan: per-device per-epoch fence: after iteration N we insert stream event, wait on host for completion then reclaim stale staging slabs. that keeps NCCL happy.

alex: propose experiment: patch allocator flags in runtime config and run repro:
```yaml
runtime:
  allocator:
    staging_pool_limit: 512MB
    slab_reclaim_iters: 32
    temp_pool_reuse: true
    ephemeral_epoch_enabled: true
    ephemeral_epoch_iters: 16
```
run perf harness with TP=8, batch 1, concurrency 4.

raj: also add a debug counter to track "staging slabs reclaimed" and "staging slabs leaked". want to see whether reclaim frequency matches reduction in committed memory.

perf-bot: noted. I'll run the CI perf job on a small fleet (3 runs) and post results.

alex: thanks — if this drops mem by ~1GB/rank and removes OOMs we can follow up with code change. otherwise next step is to instrument NCCL paths to avoid allocating temporaries in device-heap and move to preallocated comm-buffers that are reused per-epoch.

sam: thumbs up. @raj can you prototype the epoch reclaim helper? should be a small change in allocator + runtime fence logic.

raj: on it. I'll open a draft PR and ping here when ready.

alex: awesome — keeping this thread for test results. :thumbsup:
